title: React's One-Way Data Flow: Why It Matters

scenes.line1: Why does React insist on one-way data?
scenes.say: Why does React care so much about one-way data flow? What does it actually mean for your code?

scenes.label: Component
scenes.sub: Reusable UI block with its own logic
scenes.say: React apps are built from components. Each one is a reusable UI block with its own logic.
Components get data two ways: props and state. Props are read-only and come from parents. State is local and can change inside the component.
Data always flows down. Parents pass props to children. Children receive them, but can't change them. Each component manages its own state.
Here's a simple example. The parent sets the start value with props. The component manages the count with state.

scenes.question: Can a child directly change parent state?
scenes.right: No. Child can only request changes, often via callbacks passed as props.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: Can a child directly change its parent's state? No. The child can only request changes, usually through callback functions passed down as props.
